nodes.label: Module 6 — Admission, Election & Certification
nodes.rationale: Owns the regulatory state of the hospice relationship — the module a CMS surveyor opens first. The differentiator is making the regulatory state impossible to enter into a non-compliant configuration, so M23's claim layer has nothing to reject.

nodes.label: Election Period & Benefit-Period Sequencing (D9 transfer-in inheritance)
nodes.rationale: The receiving hospice inherits the period sequence per 42 CFR 418.28; restarting the counter would over-state benefit days and trigger MAC rejection at NOE submission. F2F requirements follow the inherited sequence — a 3rd-or-later period requires F2F regardless of which hospice held it.

nodes.label: Certification of Terminal Illness (CTI) with late oral-then-written path (D3, D4)
nodes.rationale: Attending signature is required on period-1 only (418.22(c) requires only the medical director on recerts). Late certs record the oral verbal cert and compute a written-cert deadline of period start + 2 calendar days; the admission is flagged but NOT auto-held because some MD signatures arrive at the 50th hour and auto-hold would create false positives.

nodes.label: Face-to-Face Encounter Compliance Artifact (D2, D5)
nodes.rationale: F2F is a compliance fact tied to 418.22(a)(4)/418.25, not just another encounter type; co-storing in M8 would force duplicating window_start/window_end/attestation/override fields onto every encounter row and lose the strict 30-day window semantics. The override lives on the F2F row itself to avoid a dual-truth 'which is the source of compliance' problem.

nodes.label: Compliance Window Engine (regulatory clocks as outbox events)
nodes.rationale: Assessment clocks live in M6 as compliance_window rows because M9 has no compliance-window primitive and M30 would otherwise query two modules to render the queue. Window math is computed in the org timezone because CMS regulation is calendar-day oriented and surveyors think in local time; UTC-only would mis-classify late certs.

nodes.label: AdmissionEventApplier (external HL7 narrow rails, D13/D14)
nodes.rationale: M6's state machines are clinical compliance artifacts; letting external input drive them would create non-repudiable survey risk (an admit not signed by the hospice MD, an F2F not attested by an NP). Permitted mutations are exactly death-discharge under strict preconditions, informational compliance windows, and referral withdrawal. Contract violations are logged and refused rather than thrown, so one partner's malformed payload cannot dead-letter the shared consumer queue for all tenants.

nodes.label: Level-of-Care Period + GIP Documentation Gate (D12)
nodes.rationale: GIP is the highest-paying and most-audited level of care; forcing the three attestations at the moment of state change creates a strong audit trail and prevents retroactive justification. Capturing documentation later in a separate flow invites surveyor findings and loses the temporal binding.

nodes.label: NOE/NOTR Wire-Artifact Ownership Belongs to M23 (D1)
nodes.rationale: NOE is a claim-adjacent artifact governed by 837I/UB-04 mechanics — billing competencies, not clinical. The clinical EHR signs the election and emits the event; the billing system tells CMS. Putting NOE in M6 would bloat it with claim-cycle state and couple it to MAC connection lifecycle.

nodes.label: For-Cause Discharge Medical-Director Cosign (D11)
nodes.rationale: For-cause discharge is the highest-risk patient-rights event in hospice operations; the medical-director cosign is both a clinical-leadership check and a survey defense. A single-step action would risk inappropriate use, and surveyors expect dual-signature evidence.
